To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the osmoprotectants TMAO and betaine protect the MscS channel of E. coli against the inhibitory effects of high hydrostatic pressure on its activity, and that the protective effect is due to the shielding of the cytoplasmically located domains of the MscS channels.
the bacterial mechanosensory channels of small conductances MscS and MscK are inhibited at HHP of up to 80 MPaa, and the osmolyte TMAO helps the channel activity at HHP of <40 MPaa.
the osmoprotectan TMAO helps the bacterial mechanosensory channel MscS/Msck to resist the effects of high pressure up to 40 MPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of high pressure on the bacterial mechanosensory channels and the possible protective role of the osmolyte TMAO.
the effect of high hydrostatic pressure on the bacterial mechanosensitivity.
the mechanism of bacterial mechanosensitive channel gating and its inhibition by high hydrostatic pressure and osmolyte.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MscS and MscK channels are inhibited under HHP and this inhibition can be partially relieved by the presence of TMAO.

TMAO protects MscS/Msk from HHP-induced inactivation at pressures below 40 MPa, and that the channels inactivate at pressures higher than 40 MPa independently of the TMAO concentration in the cytoplasm.

TMAO has an effect on the Msc channel activity at pressures up to 40 Mpa, which is the limit of the “flying patch” technique, and that at pressures above this limit the effect of TMAO on the channel is lost, and the channel is inhibited by HHP in a similar fashion as in the absence of TMAO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the osmolyte TMAO can protect the channel activity of MscS/MScK from HHP at pressures of up tp 40 MPa. Proc. SPIE
TMAO is an effective protective agent for bacterial mechanosensitive channel activity under high hydrostatic pressures.
TMAO protects MscK and MscS against the inhibitory effect caused by HHP up to a certain threshold pressure, but the mechanism of this protection is not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the osmolyte TMAO can be used as a tool to study the effect of HPP on membrane proteins.

the osmoprotectants, which are used by the cells to survive in the presence of high osmotic pressures, can also be applied to counteract the inhibitory effect on the bacterial channels of small conductances under high hydrostatic pressures.
the osmolyte TMAO protects the bacterial mechanosensory MscS/Msk channels from HHP up to a certain threshold.
